title: Cotter hole clearance
description: Cotter hole clear of the complete clamped stack. The MS9363-09 nut side is the excluded term.

checks.label: cotter hole clear of the clamped column

configuration.nut: MS9363-09 slotted -- height printed in MS9363 Rev C; castellation phase uncontrolled

excluded_terms: MS9363-09 nut height and thread-start-to-castellation distance -- the height is printed in MS9363 Rev C (spec-library subject MS9363-09, H = .178/.198 in) but deliberately not folded, because the quantity that decides cotter installability is the castellation PHASE, which no document controls (JPS00094 5.9.7's washer-swap procedure is the remedy); folding the height alone would dress an unanswerable alignment question as a linear one
checks.guidance: Head-to-cotter-hole minus the clamped column. Since 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit) the column is all five members -- the eye rides in as the loudly-marked MS14101-3 placeholder -- so what is left over must cover only the nut side: the MS9363-09's height up to a castellation slot, which stays excluded (see excluded_terms) because the slot-to-thread-start phase is uncontrolled by any document. It passes with 2.3296 mm worst case available (nominal 3.1662, max 4.3098); an MS9363-09 at its max height (5.0292 mm) does NOT fit inside the worst-case budget, which is the castellation/washer-selection story again, not a new finding. It cannot settle the joint either way: with a slotted nut and a cotter pin the constraint is slot-vs-hole ALIGNMENT, which quantises acceptable grip -- see the referenced stack's notes. This guidance is a copy of the stack's own, kept in step by hand.

provenance.equivalent_to: check `cotter_hole_clear_of_sourced_stack` of docs/tolerance_stacks/stack_pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.json (which folds path `head_to_cotter_hole` minus path `clamped_stack_sourced`)
provenance.pinned_by: tests/test_topology_conversions.py -- every field of the folded interval must equal that check's, exactly.

notes: The selection combines both stack paths this check needs (`head_to_cotter_hole` and `clamped_stack_sourced`) into ONE chain rather than composing two separately-summed StudyResults, because this topology puts every dimension on one connected graph -- there is no cross-study composition here for `docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md`'s fenced deliverable-4 concern to apply to.

The chain walks `cotter_hole_from_point` AGAINST its authored orientation (bolt_point -> cotter_hole_centerline, sign -1, i.e. it enters this study reversed), then `bolt_length_11` WITH its orientation (head_bearing_face -> bolt_point, sign -1 relative to this study's direction... entered from bolt_point going to head_bearing_face, i.e. against its own authored direction, sign -1 contributing +bolt_length_11 when read from this study's from-node), then the three clamped edges WITH their authored orientation (sign +1 each). Read end to end from `washer_far_face`: +washer, +pitch_plate_flange, +bushing_214820 is the wrong order to state signs in prose -- the authoritative signs are whatever `traverse()` derives from the graph, and `tests/test_topology_conversions.py` pins the resulting total against the stack's own published check rather than trusting this paragraph.
